condition: Rectal cancer — palpable rectal mass with a negative FIT
permutationLabel: FIT < 10 but rectal mass on DRE
summary: 71-year-old man with tenesmus and a hard irregular rectal mass 6 cm from the anal verge; FIT 6 µg Hb/g. A rectal mass is referred regardless of the FIT (BSG/ACPGBI 2022); MRI pelvis for local staging.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Feeling of incomplete emptying of the bowel
inputs.hpi: Two months of feeling he has not finished after opening his bowels, going 3–4 times each morning. Occasional mucus. No visible blood. Weight steady. GP FIT 6 µg Hb/g, reported as negative. Hypertension.

exam.abdomen: Soft, non-tender, no mass. PR: hard, irregular, fixed rectal mass on the anterior wall, lower edge 6 cm from the anal verge; no blood on the glove.
exam.other: Rigid sigmoidoscopy: ulcerated tumour at 6–10 cm.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Rectal mass — suspected rectal cancer
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Hard, fixed rectal mass at 6 cm on DRE with a negative FIT. Suspected rectal cancer: biopsy, MRI pelvis, CT chest/abdomen/pelvis, colonoscopy; colorectal MDT.

mustInclude.note: MRI pelvis for T/N stage, CRM and EMVI before any treatment decision.

guideline.name: ACPGBI/BSG joint guideline — FIT in patients with signs or symptoms of suspected colorectal cancer
guideline.section: Patients with a rectal or abdominal mass, anal ulceration or IDA are referred irrespective of the FIT result
guideline.citation: Monahan KJ, Davies MM, Abulafi M, et al. Faecal immunochemical testing (FIT) in patients with signs or symptoms of suspected colorectal cancer (CRC): a joint guideline from the Association of Coloproctology of Great Britain and Ireland (ACPGBI) and the British Society of Gastroenterology (BSG). Gut. 2022;71:1939–1962.

guideline.name: NICE NG12 — suspected cancer: recognition and referral (lower gastrointestinal tract cancers)
guideline.section: Lower GI: consider suspected cancer pathway referral for a rectal or abdominal mass
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Suspected cancer: recognition and referral (NG12). First published 2015; lower GI recommendations updated 2023 to incorporate DG56.

rationale: Permutation: FIT below threshold, but a hard rectal mass on examination. The DRE finding is written in the abdominal examination field (where many clinicians record PR), because the web Anal/Rectal examination section is not read by the clinical prompts.

authoring.author: Claude (colorectal/anorectal cluster)
authoring.notes: Expectations need surgeon sign-off (reviewedBy). Citations verified: false until checked against the source.
